beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:enticing, setting the scene][tune:level]On the islands of ^Malta, in the middle of the Mediterranean: stone temples ^older than the pyramids. [act:lower, a little eerie][tune:level]An underground city of the ^dead. [act:the tantalising one, hushed][tune:fall]And stories of sanctuaries under the ^sea.

[d:calm][act:grounded, admiring]Ġgantija stands on ^Gozo, the little island next to Malta. [act:grounded, a sense of scale]Its walls still rise six metres high: about two storeys of a ^house@noun. [act:grounded, precise]It was built around {3600|thirty-six hundred} BCE. [go:2|0][act:letting it sink in, wonder]Centuries ^older than Egypt's pyramids. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a sense of time]When its first stones went up, the pyramids were still about a thousand years in the ^future.

[d:build][act:fair, presenting the bold idea]The writer Graham ^Hancock goes ^further: maybe the temples are far older, from the ^Ice Age, when the sea stood lower, with more of them now under ^water.
[d:build][act:storytelling, adventurous]In his {2002|two thousand two} book, ^Underworld, he described diving off the coast after a reported ^underwater temple.

[d:build][act:methodical, stacking the evidence]But the evidence stacks ^up. [p:0.93][act:explaining, the key logic]Anything sealed beneath a floor is older than the floor, so charcoal and bone from beneath the temples show the earliest they could have been ^built. [act:methodical]Add the changing styles of the pottery, and the older farm villages the temples were built ^over. [act:landing it, clear][tune:fall]It all points between {3600|thirty-six hundred} and {2500|twenty-five hundred} BCE.

[d:build][go:5|0][act:with care, quiet]The ^Hypogeum, the underground city of the dead, cut three levels deep into the rock, held the remains of some seven thousand ^people. [act:with care, quiet][tune:fall]They belong to the ^same age.

[d:reveal][act:the twist, leaning in]And yet, in {2025|twenty twenty-five}, the experts were ^surprised. [act:vivid, full of wonder]^Hunter-gatherers, people who lived by hunting and gathering, reached Malta about eighty-five hundred years ago, across a ^hundred kilometres of open sea.
[d:build][sfx:hit][act:the payoff, firm][tune:fall]A ^thousand years ^before the first farmers came over from ^Sicily.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]^Ice Age temples? [act:the verdict, firm and exact]*Ruled ^out*: ^nothing from them is older than about {3600|thirty-six hundred} BCE. [act:brightening, curious][tune:rise]An ^older Malta? [act:delighted, open][tune:fall]Still being ^found.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:warm, a gentle smile]Older than the pyramids is ^already astonishing.
